reason: Checked against the source. take_off (render.6502 1288) begins LDA need,X / BPL out / RTS, so an entry whose need bit 7 is clear does nothing there. The new LDA need,X / BPL makes the same test and has no side effect, and need is zero page (&1F+), so ROMSEL, ANDY and ACCCON X do not affect it. Control flow: act_n is at most MOVER_SLOTS (&22), so Y never reaches 128 and BMI fires only when DEY wraps 0 to &FF after a skipped entry at index 0. In the original, LDY ren_k = 0 falls out at that point. The player (X=0) is still caught by BEQ before the need read. A stale entry at index 0 goes STY ren_k=0, then the unchanged tail falls out. The one state difference is ren_k at taken_off: the original always left 0 there, the new code leaves the last stale index. Grep shows ren_k is used only in render.6502, and every later reader (apply_entries 499/509, mark_to_draw, close_over_overlaps) writes it before reading it. It sits in ren_zp (&1F-&75), which the game logic does not use, so nothing sees the difference. No generated source, table, raster-timed code or protected line is touched. Cycles for a skipped entry: original DEY2 STY3 LDX4 BEQ2 JSR6 LDA4 BPL3 RTS6 LDY3 BNE3 = 36, new DEY2 BMI2 LDX4 BEQ2 LDA4 BPL3 = 17, saving 19. A stale entry costs 8 cycles more (BMI2 LDA4 BPL2). Size is 6 bytes larger (not smaller). Bank 4's tightest current listings are DEBUG_FULLREDRAW, ending at &B3F9 (7 bytes free), and gameplay/hud_rupture, ending at &B3F6 (10 free), so 6 bytes fit in every build, but only if earlier applied candidates in this batch have not used that room. Page crossings after the shift are left to the gate.
